intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 nonsense mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (orofacial cleft-7; OFC7), which is included here.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous loss-of-function mutations of the poliovirus receptor-like 1 (PVRL1) gene encoding nectin-1.
checks.explanation: PVRL1 is the former symbol for NECTIN1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state the chromosomal location. The claim only adds the gene's standard location to the gene the paper identifies, which the instructions count as supported nomenclature.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 nonsense mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The mutation referred to is the PVRL1 (NECTIN1) nonsense mutation W185X. The OFC7 label is the OMIM entry name, not a factual claim about the paper.

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families on Margarita Island in northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State). The families were probably related to each other. The patients had ectodermal dysplasia and other anomalies, and females were affected as severely as males. Expressivity was variable. All parents were normal. The authors reported that the clinical picture shared by all patients did not fit any of the known ectodermal dysplasias and did not resemble previously published cases.

paragraphs.text: Yoshida et al. (2015) studied a 7-year-old Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome who was born to consanguineous parents. His features included hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, hypodontia, cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers, mild mental retardation, and pili torti. They found a homozygous c.400C-T transition in exon 2 of the NECTIN1 gene, resulting in an arg134-to-ter (R134X) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous for the mutation.
